<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">
<div></div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">The criteria for classifying leases as finance or operating leases depend on the substance of the agreements and are made at the inception of the lease in accordance with the following principles as set out in IAS 17.</div>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt"><u>The Group as lessee:</u></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="ze2b86c6d62994dbfbef740125810bbd7" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 84.95pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 27.35pt; vertical-align: top">1.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Finance lease</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">Finance leases transfer to the Company substantially all the risks and benefits incidental to ownership of the leased asset. At the commencement of the lease term, the leased assets are measured at the fair value of the leased asset or, if lower, at the present value of the minimum lease payments.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman,Times,serif; margin: 0px 0px 0px 113.4pt; text-align: justify">The leased asset is depreciated over the shorter of the lease term and the expected life of the leased asset.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="z766990d609d843d49f77b2f5071224b0" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 84.95pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 27.35pt; vertical-align: top">2.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Operating lease</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">Lease agreements are classified as an operating lease if they do not transfer substantially all the risks and benefits incidental to ownership of the leased asset. Lease payments are recognized as an expense in profit or loss on a straight-line basis over the lease term.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="z4983a771cddf48a886d45372d000a50f" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 56.9pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 26.65pt; vertical-align: top">m.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Property, plant and equipment</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">Property, plant and equipment are measured at cost, including directly attributable costs and financing costs, less accumulated depreciation, accumulated impairment losses and any related investment grants and excluding day-to-day servicing expenses. Cost includes spare parts and auxiliary equipment that can be used only in connection with the plant and equipment.</div>



<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The Company's assets include computer systems comprising hardware and software. Software forming an integral part of the hardware to the extent that the hardware cannot function without the software installed on it is classified as property, plant and equipment. In contrast, software that adds functionality to the hardware is classified as an intangible asset.</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt"><br />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The cost of assets includes the cost of materials, direct labor costs, as well as any costs directly attributable to bringing the asset to the location and condition necessary for it to operate in the manner intended by management.</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt"><br />
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The useful life, depreciation method and residual value of an asset are reviewed at the year-end and any changes are accounted for prospectively as a change in accounting estimate.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt; line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">Depreciation of an asset ceases at the earlier of the date that the asset is classified as held for sale and the date that the asset is derecognized.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="z147ca8883f634ab19671c63684598af4" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 56.9pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 26.65pt; vertical-align: top">n.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Impairment of non-financial assets</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The Company evaluates the need to record an impairment of the carrying amount of non-financial assets whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount is not recoverable. If the carrying amount of non-financial assets exceeds their recoverable amount, the assets are reduced to their recoverable amount.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The recoverable amount is the higher of fair value less costs of sale and value in use. In measuring value in use, the expected future cash flows are discounted using a pre-tax discount rate that reflects the risks specific to the asset. The recoverable amount of an asset that does not generate independent cash flows is determined for the cash-generating unit to which the asset belongs.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">An impairment loss of an asset, is reversed only if there have been changes in the estimates used to determine the asset's recoverable amount since the last impairment loss was recognized. Reversal of an impairment loss, as above, shall not be increased above the lower of the carrying amount that would have been determined (net of depreciation or amortization) had no impairment loss been recognized for the asset in prior years and its recoverable amount.</div>



<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="zb513d97b6e0742d99ae5828d7b6cbd77" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">

<td style="width: 56.9pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 26.65pt; vertical-align: top">o.</td>

<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Financial instruments</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">
<div></div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt; text-indent: 0pt">Regarding the initial adoption of IFRS 9, "Financial Instruments" ("the Standard"), the Company elected to adopt the provisions of the Standard retrospectively without restatement of comparative data.</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt; text-indent: 0pt">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="z43000ddcc8ba4bbc9d415178e84953c4" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 84.95pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 27.35pt; vertical-align: top">1.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Financial assets</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">Financial </font>assets are classified, at initial recognition, and subsequently measured at amortized cost, fair value through other comprehensive income (OCI), and fair value through profit or loss. The classification of financial assets at initial recognition depends on the financial asset&#8217;s contractual cash flow characteristics and the Company&#8217;s business model for managing them. With the exception of trade receivables that do not contain a significant financing component or for which the Company has applied the practical expedient, the Company initially measures a financial asset at its fair value plus, in the case of a financial asset not at fair value through profit or loss, transaction costs.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">After initial recognition, the accounting treatment of financial assets is based on their classification as follows:</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">Debt financial instruments are subsequently measured at fair value through profit or loss (FVPL), amortized cost, or fair value through other comprehensive income (FVOCI). The classification is based on two criteria: the Company&#8217;s business model for managing the assets; and whether the instruments&#8217; contractual cash flows represent &#8216;solely payments of principal and interest&#8217; on the principal amount outstanding (the &#8216;SPPI criterion&#8217;).</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt"><br />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">The classification and measurement of the Company&#8217;s debt financial assets are as follows:</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="zbe0ed6f714584cf4bd355f84c2deda55" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 114.75pt"><br />
</td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 18pt; vertical-align: top">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">Debt instruments at amortized cost for financial assets that are held within a business model with the objective to hold the financial assets in order to collect contractual cash flows that meet the SPPI criterion. This category includes the Company&#8217;s Trade and other receivables.</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="z613b2b145e9947248e42967ab1f2da45" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 114.75pt"><br />
</td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 18pt; vertical-align: top">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">Debt instruments at FVOCI, with gains or losses recycled to profit or loss on derecognition. Financial assets in this category are the Company&#8217;s quoted debt instruments that meet the SPPI criterion and are held within a business model both to collect cash flows and to sell. <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">Interest earned whilst holding AFS financial investments is reported as interest income using the effective interest rate method.</font></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">Financial assets at FVPL comprise derivative </font>instruments unless they are designated as effective hedging instruments.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: left; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="za72aedd7a2ce4374863e03dff064a8a4" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr style="height: 5px">
<td style="width: 114.75pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 18pt; vertical-align: top">a.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: left">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">&#160;Impairment of financial assets</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">
<div></div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 136.6pt"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">The Company assesses at the end of each reporting period whether there is any objective evidence of impairment of a financial asset or group of financial assets. The Company records an allowance for </font><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">expected credit loss </font><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">("ECL") for all debt financial assets not held at FVPL.</font></div>
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 136.6pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 136.6pt">ECLs are based on the difference between the contractual cash flows due in accordance with the contract and all the cash flows that the Company expects to receive. For other debt financial assets (i.e., debt securities at FVOCI), the ECL is based on the 12-month ECL. The 12-month ECL is the portion of lifetime ECLs that results from default events on a financial instrument that are possible within 12 months after the reporting date. As of December 31, 2018 there is no ECL allowance.<br />
</div>
</div>



<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="z20d2b6c8d1fe4fcabe6c40fbbecc298b" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 84pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 28.5pt; vertical-align: top">2.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Financial liabilities</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.55pt">Financial liabilities within the scope of IFRS 9 are initially measured at fair value.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.55pt">After initial recognition, the accounting treatment of financial liabilities is based on their classification as follows:</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt; line-height: 1.25"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">a.</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Financial liabilities measured at amortized cost</u></font></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 144pt; line-height: 1.25">Loans, including capital leases, are measured based on their terms at amortized cost using the effective interest method taking into account directly attributable transaction costs. </div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt; line-height: 1.25"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">b.</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Financial liabilities measured at fair value</u></font></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman,Times,serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 144pt">Derivatives are classified as fair value through profit and loss unless they are designated as effective hedging instruments. Transaction costs are recognized in profit or loss.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 56.7pt; line-height: 1.25; text-indent: 28.35pt"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">3.</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <font style="font: normal 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Fair value measurement</u></font></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">Fair value is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">
<div></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">Fair value measurement is based on the assumption that the transaction will take place in the asset's or the liability's principal market, or in the absence of a principal market, in the most advantageous market.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">The fair value of an asset or a liability is measured using the assumptions that market participants would use when pricing the asset or liability, assuming that market participants act in their economic best interest.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">A fair value measurement of a non-financial asset takes into account a market participant's ability to generate economic benefits by using the asset in its highest and best use or by selling it to another market participant that would use the asset in its highest and best use.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">The Company uses valuation techniques that are appropriate in the circumstances and for which sufficient data are available to measure fair value, maximizing the use of relevant observable inputs and minimizing the use of unobservable inputs.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">All assets and liabilities for which fair value is measured or disclosed in the financial statements are categorized within the fair value hierarchy, described as follows, based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement as a whole:</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="z1da910b2d347433bb4c35cb1a75a339c" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 113.4pt"><br />
</td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 14.2pt; vertical-align: top">-</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">Level 1 - quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="ze3f6da04c5a1457699134e8b90d2e85d" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 113.4pt"><br />
</td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 14.2pt; vertical-align: top">-</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">Level 2 - inputs other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable either directly or indirectly.</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="z3f704876f1ad4ff6bd79bdcea72241fb" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 113.4pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 14.2pt; vertical-align: top">-</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">Level 3 - inputs that are not based on observable market data (valuation techniques which use inputs that are not based on observable market data).</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>



<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt; line-height: 1.25"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">4.</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Offsetting financial instruments</u></font></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">Financial assets and financial liabilities are offset and the net amount is presented in the statement of financial position if there is a legally enforceable right to set off the recognized amounts and there is an intention either to settle on a net basis or to realize the asset and settle the liability simultaneously.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">The right of set-off must be legally enforceable not only during the ordinary course of business of the parties to the contract but also in the event of bankruptcy or insolvency of one of the parties. In order for the right of set-off to be currently available, it must not be contingent on a future event, there may not be periods during which the right is not available, or there may not be any events that will cause the right to expire.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt; line-height: 1.25"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">5.</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>De-recognition of financial instruments</u></font></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt; line-height: 1.25"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">a.</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Financial assets</u></font></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 141.75pt">Financial assets are derecognized when the contractual rights to the cash flows from the financial asset expire or the Company has transferred its contractual rights to receive cash flows from the financial asset or assumes an obligation to pay the cash flows in full without material delay to a third party and has transferred substantially all the risks and rewards of the asset, or has neither transferred nor retained substantially all the risks and rewards of the asset, but has transferred control of the asset.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt; line-height: 1.25"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">b.</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Financial liabilities</u></font></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 141.75pt; line-height: 1.25"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">A financial liability is derecognized when it is extinguished, that is when the obligation is discharged or cancelled or expires. A financial liability is extinguished when the debtor (the Company) discharges the</font><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"> liability by paying in cash, other financial assets, goods or services or is legally released from the liability.</font></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="z0cd256c7aec5480ca0664b0b35fe0361" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 56.9pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 26.65pt; vertical-align: top">p.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Derivative financial instruments designated as hedges</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The Company enters into contracts for derivative financial instruments such as forward currency contracts and cylinder strategy in respect of foreign currency to hedge risks associated with foreign exchange rates fluctuations. Such derivative financial instruments are carried as financial assets when the fair value is positive and as financial liabilities when the fair value is negative.</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt"><br />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">At the inception of a hedge relationship, the Company formally designates and documents the hedge relationship to which the Company wishes to apply hedge accounting and the risk management objective and strategy for undertaking the hedge. The hedge effectiveness is assessed at the end of each reporting period.</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: left">
<div></div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">Any gains or losses arising from changes in the fair value of derivatives that do not qualify for hedge accounting are recorded immediately in profit or loss.</div>
</div>



<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt"><u>Cash flow hedges</u></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The effective portion of the gain or loss on the hedging instrument is recognized as other comprehensive income (loss), while any ineffective portion is recognized immediately in profit or loss.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">Amounts recognized as other comprehensive income (loss) are reclassified to profit or loss when the hedged transaction affects profit or loss, such as when the hedged income or expense is recognized or when a forecast payment occurs.</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt"><br />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">If the forecast transaction or firm commitment is no longer expected to occur, amounts previously recognized in other comprehensive income are reclassified to profit or loss. If the hedging instrument expires or is sold, terminated or exercised, or if its designation as a hedge is revoked, amounts previously recognized in other comprehensive income remain in other comprehensive income until the forecast transaction or firm commitment occurs.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="zd2ceafd04b52447f93a49046f9d5f291" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 56.9pt"></td>
<td style="width: 26.65pt; vertical-align: top; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">q.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Accrued expenses</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">A provision in accordance with IAS 37 is recognized when the Group has a present (legal or constructive) obligation as a result of a past event, it is expected to require the use of economic resources to clear the obligation and a reliable estimate can be made of it.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="za501a8d100cb45169f76cb6c7afe8e3f" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 56.9pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 26.65pt; vertical-align: top">r.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Employee benefit liabilities</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt"><br />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The Company has several employee benefit plans:</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="zf86e0da5d68d49f69a1707e2b57b66fd" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 84.95pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 27.35pt; vertical-align: top">1.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Short-term employee benefits</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">Short-term employee benefits include salaries, paid annual leave, paid sick leave, recreation and social security contributions and are recognized as expenses as the services are rendered. A liability in respect of a cash bonus is recognized when the Company has a legal or constructive obligation to make such payment as a result of past service rendered by an employee and a reliable estimate of the amount can be made.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="za53ff84547994551b039303750bb6ce3" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 84.95pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 27.35pt; vertical-align: top">2.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Post-employment benefits</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">The post-employment benefits plans are normally financed by contributions to insurance companies and classified as defined contribution plans or as defined benefit plans.</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt"><br />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">The Company has defined contribution plans pursuant to Section 14 to the Israeli Severance Pay Law under which the Company pays fixed contributions to certain employees under section 14 and will have no legal or constructive obligation to pay further contributions.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">Contributions to the defined contribution plan in respect of severance or retirement pay are recognized as an expense when contributed concurrently with performance of the employee's services.</div>



<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">In addition the Company operates a defined benefit plan in respect of severance pay pursuant to the Israeli Severance Pay Law. According to the Law, employees are entitled to severance pay upon dismissal or retirement. The liability for termination of employment is measured using the projected unit credit method. The actuarial assumptions include expected salary increases and rates of employee's turnover based on the estimated timing of payment. The amounts are presented based on discounted expected future cash flows using a discount rate determined by reference to market yields at the reporting date on high quality corporate bonds that are linked to the Consumer Price Index with a term that is consistent with the estimated term of the severance pay obligation.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">In respect of its severance pay obligation to certain of its employees, the Company makes current deposits in pension funds and insurance companies ("the plan assets"). Plan assets comprise assets held by a long-term employee benefit fund or qualifying insurance policies. Plan assets are not available to the Company's own creditors and cannot be returned directly to the Company.</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt"><br />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">The liability for employee benefits shown in the statement of financial position reflects the present value of the defined benefit obligation less the fair value of the plan assets.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">Re-measurements of the net liability are recognized in other comprehensive income in the period in which they occur.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="za29c42829008493f91febe8e0293a046" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 56.9pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 26.65pt; vertical-align: top">s.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Share-based payment transactions</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The Company's employees and Board of Directors members are entitled to remuneration in the form of equity-settled share-based payment transactions.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt; line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt"><u>Equity-settled transactions</u></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The cost of equity-settled transactions (options and restricted shares) with employees and Board of Directors members is measured at the fair value of the equity instruments granted at grant date. The fair value of options is determined using a standard option pricing model. The fair value of restricted shares is determined using the share price at the grant date.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The cost of equity-settled transactions is recognized in profit or loss together with a corresponding increase in shareholder's equity during the period which the performance and/or service conditions are to be satisfied ending on the date on which the relevant employees become entitled to the award ("the vesting period"). The cumulative expense recognized for equity-settled transactions at the end of each reporting period until the vesting date reflects the extent to which the vesting period has expired and the Company&#8217;s best estimate of the number of equity instruments that will ultimately vest.</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt"><br />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">No expense is recognized for awards that do not ultimately vest.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">In the event that the Company modifies the conditions on which equity-instruments were granted, an additional expense is calculated and recognized<font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">&#160;</font>over the remaining vesting period for any modification that increases the total fair value of the share-based payment arrangement or is otherwise beneficial to the employee/ Director at the modification date.</div>



<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="z1bf2a9351a75449f96a2738b86b13748" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr style="height: 14px">
<td style="width: 56.9pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 26.65pt; vertical-align: top">t.</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">&#160;&#160;&#160;<u>Earnings (loss) per Share</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; margin: 0px 0px 0px 92.15pt; text-align: justify">Earnings (loss) per share are calculated by dividing the net income (loss) attributable to Company shareholders by the weighted number of ordinary shares outstanding during the period. Ordinary shares underlying shares options or restricted shares are only included in the calculation of diluted income (loss) per share when their impact dilutes the income (loss) per share. <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">Furthermore, potential ordinary shares converted during the period are included under diluted income (loss) per share only until the conversion date, and from that date on are included under basic income (loss) per share.</font></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div></div></div><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
</table>

<th class="tl" colspan="1" rowspan="2"><div style="width: 200px;"><strong>SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING JUDGMENTS, ESTIMATES AND ASSUMPTIONS USED IN THE PREPARATION OF THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS<br></strong></div></th>
<th class="th" colspan="1">12 Months Ended</th>
</tr>
<tr><th class="th"><div>Dec. 31, 2018</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_kmda_DisclosureOfSignificantAccountingJudgmentsEstimatesAndAssumptionsUsedInPreparationOfFinancialStatementsAbstract', window );"><strong>Disclosure of significant accounting judgments, estimates and assumptions used in the preparation of the financial statements [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_ifrs-full_DisclosureOfAccountingJudgementsAndEstimatesExplanatory', window );">SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING JUDGMENTS, ESTIMATES AND ASSUMPTIONS USED IN THE PREPARATION OF THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</a></td>
<td class="text"><div><div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25"><table id="zf161e2c617fe4495abb982f55d1344a9" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="font: small-caps bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; vertical-align: top; width: 54pt">Note 3: -</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify; width: auto">
<div style="font: small-caps bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">&#160;Significant accounting judgments, estimates and assumptions used in the preparation of the financial statements</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">
<div id="DSPFPageHeader"></div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 56.7pt">In the process of applying the significant accounting policies, the Group has made the following judgments which have the most significant effect on the amounts recognized in the financial statements:</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 56.7pt">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="z0face79c984948c48d14b8658fb37a0b" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 56.9pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; vertical-align: top; width: 26.65pt">a.</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify; width: auto">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">&#160;&#160; <u>Judgments</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 92.15pt"><u>Revenue</u></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 92.15pt">The Company assesses the criteria for recognition of revenue related to up-front payments and milestones as outlined by IFRS 15. Judgment is necessary to determine over which period the Company will satisfy its performance obligations related to up-front payments and milestones and whether financing component exists. For additional information, refer to Note 17a.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="z785130d5dec644a9b85392d567770e39" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 56.9pt"></td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 26.65pt"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">b</font><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">.</font></td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify; width: auto">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">&#160; <u>Estimates and assumptions</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">
<div></div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 92.15pt">The preparation of the financial statements requires management to make estimates and assumptions that have an effect on the application of the accounting policies and on the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses. Changes in accounting estimates are reported in the period of the change in estimate.</div>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 92.15pt">The key assumptions made in the financial statements concerning uncertainties at the end of the reporting period and the critical estimates computed by the Company that may result in a material adjustment to the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities within the next financial year are discussed below.<br />
<br />
</div>

<div>
<table id="z8be931de24b94cb5a7ce46fb18acd0cc" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 108.7pt">
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: left; margin-left: 90.7pt">-</div>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: auto">
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify"><u>Legal claims</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<br />
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; margin: 0px 0px 0px 109.25pt; text-align: justify">In estimating the likelihood of outcome of legal claims filed against the Company, the Company relies on the opinion of its legal counsel. These estimates are based on the legal counsel's best professional judgment, taking into account the stage of proceedings and historical legal precedents in respect of the different issues. Since the outcome of the claims will be determined in courts, the results could differ from these estimates.</div>

<p class="3" style="margin-left: 108.7pt; text-indent: -18pt; mso-pagination: widow-orphan; mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: 106.35pt"><font lang="X-NONE" style="line-height: 110%; mso-list: Ignore; mso-bidi-font-size: 11.0pt; mso-bidi-font-family: Times New Roman">-<font style="font: 7pt Times New Roman">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></font><u style="line-height: 110%; mso-bidi-font-size: 11.0pt">Pensions and other post-employment benefits</u></p>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; margin: 0px 0px 0px 109.25pt; text-align: justify">The liability in respect of post-employment defined benefit plans is determined using actuarial valuations. The actuarial valuation involves making assumptions about, among others, discount rates, expected rates of return on assets, future salary increases and mortality rates. Due to the long-term nature of these plans, such estimates are subject to significant uncertainty.</div>



<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div>
<table id="z45ac91febbef475097526cacf2d4688d" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 90pt">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 18pt">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman,Times,serif">-</div>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: auto">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman,Times,serif"><u>Determining the fair value of share-based payment transactions</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 110.55pt">Estimating fair value for share-based payment transactions requires determination of the most <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">appropriate</font> valuation model, which depends on the terms and conditions of the grant. This estimate also requires determination of the most appropriate inputs to the valuation model including the expected life of the share option or appreciation right, volatility and dividend yield and making assumptions about them.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div>
<table id="z7ffab63cb48949ab9e5b805b02d3d634" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 108.7pt">
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: left; margin-left: 90.7pt">-</div>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: auto">
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify"><u>Provisions for clinical trial and related expenses</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 110.55pt">Accrued expenses costs for clinical trial activities performed by third parties, are based on estimates on the progress of completion of the clinical trials or services, as of the end of each reporting period, pursuant to the contract with the third parties, and the agreed upon fee to be paid for such services.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div>
<table id="z22af40a83d5e420094942134eab9f4e4" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 108.7pt">
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: left; margin-left: 90.7pt">-</div>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: auto">
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify"><u>Capitalization of materials for clinical trials and inventory designated for R&#38;D activities</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 110.55pt">The Company recognizes inventory produced for commercial sale, including costs incurred prior to regulatory approval but subsequent to the filing of a regulatory request when the Company has determined that the inventory has probable future economic benefit. Inventory is not recognized prior to completion of a phase III clinical trial. For products with an approved indication, raw materials and purchased drug product associated with development programs are included in inventory and charged to research and development expense when consumed. For products without an approved indication, drug product is charged to research and development expense.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div>
<table id="z8ebb7e8e32834ef8b1a1a50aaf2c1254" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 108.7pt">
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: left; margin-left: 90.7pt">-</div>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: auto">
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify"><u>Recognition </u><u>of deferred tax asset in respect of carry forward tax losses</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">
<div></div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 108.25pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 108.25pt">The Company recorded a deferred tax asset in respect of carry forward tax losses based on effective tax rate calculation considering the Law for the Encouragement of Capital Investments and future taxable income estimation and the probability that in the future there will be taxable income against which the carry forwards losses can be utilized. This estimation can affect the recognition or reversal of deferred tax asset in the profit or loss. For information regarding deferred taxes recognition, please refer to note 21.</div>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div>
<table id="zfe267bb0ea7f4e40bdf04c5665ac1031" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 108.7pt">
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: left; margin-left: 90.7pt">-</div>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: auto">
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify"><u>Impairment test for the production facility</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 108.25pt">The Company performed an impairment test due to indications that can, in the future, result in a possible impairment. The Company calculated the recoverable amount of the production facility to determine whether the book value exceeds its recoverable amount. The impairment test was based on a DCF model using the Company's long term forecast. As of December 31, 2018 no impairment was recorded as the recoverable amount exceeded the book value.</div>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">
<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />

</div></div><span></span>
</td>
</tr>

</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_ifrs-full_StatementOfIFRSCompliance', window );">DISCLUSURE OF NEW STANDARDS IN THE PERIOD PRIOR TO THEIR ADOPTION</a></td>
<td class="text"><div id="DSPFPageHeader"><div><div style="line-height: 1.25"><div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25"><table id="z46b414bd6a2745448e2d1e1e814a1b9c" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%"><tr><td style="font: small-caps bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; vertical-align: top; width: 54pt">Note 4: -</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify; width: auto">
<div style="font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">&#160;DISCLUSURE OF NEW <font style="font: small-caps 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">STANDARDS IN THE PERIOD PRIOR TO THEIR ADOPTION</font></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="ze0746e13da6a427d8b14f96271a1615b" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 56.9pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; vertical-align: top; width: 26.65pt">a.</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify; width: auto">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>IFRS 16 &#8211; Leases</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt"><br />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">IFRS 16, replaces IAS 17 (Leases), and affects the accounting treatment for lessees with respect to leased assets. Pursuant to IFRS 16, all leases (except short term leases and small asset leases) will be recognized in the balance sheet. Initially, the lease liability and the right-of-use asset are measured at the present value of future lease payments (defined as economically unavoidable payments). The right-of-use asset is subsequently depreciated in a similar way to other assets such as tangible assets, i.e. typically in a straight-line over the lease term. Lessees will be required to separately recognize the interest expense on the lease liability and the depreciation expense on the right-of-use asset. Lessees will be also required to re-measure the lease liability upon the occurrence of certain events (e.g., a change in the lease term, a change in future lease payments resulting from a change in an index or rate used to determine those payments). The lessee will generally recognize the amount of the re-measurement of the lease liability as an adjustment to the right-of-use asset.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br />
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The new Standard is effective for annual periods be<font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; background-color: #ffffff">ginning on or after January 1, 2019. Earlier </font>application<font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; background-color: #ffffff"> is permitted provided that IFRS 15, "Revenue from Contracts with Customers", is applied concurrently.</font></div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The Company plans to adopt IFRS 16 using the cumulative effect method without changing comparative information. <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; background-color: #ffffff">The</font> cumulative impact will adjust the opening balance of the equity at the date of initial application (i.e. January 1, 2019). The Company elects to apply the standard to contracts that were previously identified as leases applying IAS 17. The Company will therefore not apply the standard to contracts that were not previously identified as containing a lease applying IAS 17.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The Company elects to use the exemptions proposed by the standard with respect to lease contracts for which the underlying asset is of low value. The Company has leases of certain office equipment (i.e., printing and photocopying machines) that are considered of low value.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">During 2018, the Company has performed a detailed impact assessment of IFRS 16. Impact on the statement of financial position (increase/(decrease)) as at January 1, 2019:</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">
<div>
<div></div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 78pt">Pursuant to the adoption of IFRS 16, the Company&#8217;s operating expenses will be changed by the difference between the previously recognized lease costs and the depreciation costs on account of the Right-of-Use assets. In addition, the Company will begin to recognize interest expenses regarding the lease liability, which were not recognized in prior periods. Moreover, as of December 31, 2018 the effect of the initial adoption of the new Standard in 2019 is expected to result in a decrease in the Company's lease expenses of $967 thousands and an increase in the Company's depreciation and finance expenses of $804 thousands and $185 thousands, respectively. The total effect of the initial adoption of the new Standard in 2019 is expected to result in an increase of $163 thousands in operating income and a decrease of $22 thousands in income before taxes.</div>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">&#160;</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="z4178c9d2ad8b45948ac475d67ba27d2a" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">
<tr>
<td style="width: 56.9pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; vertical-align: top; width: 26.65pt">b.</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify; width: auto">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>IFRIC 23 - Uncertainty over Income Tax Treatment</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">IFRIC 23 clarifies application of recognition and measurement requirements in IAS 12 (Income Taxes) when there is uncertainty over income tax treatment. In determining taxable profit (tax loss), tax bases, unused tax losses, unused tax credits and tax rates, an entity must consider the probability that a taxation authority will accept an uncertain tax treatment. An entity has to determine whether to consider each uncertain tax treatment separately or together with one or more other uncertain tax treatments. The approach that better predicts the resolution of the uncertainty should be followed.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">IFRIC 23 is effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2019. The Company will apply the interpretation from its effective date.&#160; The Company evaluated the possible impact of IFRIC 23, reviewed its tax position taken, in the Company's tax returns for all tax years currently open to examination by a taxing authority. <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; background-color: #ffffff">The Company believes the implementation of </font>IFRIC 23 <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; background-color: #ffffff">is not expected to have a material impact on its financial statements.</font></div>

</div></div></div></div><span></span>
</td>
</tr>

                        reclassified from FVTPL to FVOCI as of January 1, 2018.</font></div></td></tr></table></div></div></div></div></div><span></span>
</td>
</tr>

<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Financial risk factors</u></div>
</td>
</tr>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The Company's activities expose it to various financial risks, such as market risk (<font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">foreign</font> currency risk, interest rate risk and price risk), credit risk and liquidity risk. The Company's investment policy focuses on activities that will preserve the Company's capital. The Company utilized derivatives to hedge certain exposures to risk.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">Risk management is the responsibility of the Company CEO and CFO, in accordance with the </font>policy<font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"> approved by the Board of Directors. The Board of Directors provides principles for the overall risk management.</font></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt; line-height: 1.25"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">1.</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Market risks</u></font></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">
<table id="za31eb0235aa045c9b16093d17e45fa51" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 100%">

<td style="width: 113.4pt"></td>
<td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif; width: 28.35pt; vertical-align: top">a)</td>
<td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">&#160;<u>Foreign exchange risk</u></div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 144.6pt">The Company operates in an international environment and is exposed to foreign exchange risk resulting from the exposure to different currencies, mainly the NIS and EUR. Foreign exchange risks arise from recognized assets and liabilities denominated in a foreign currency other than the functional currency, such as trade and other accounts receivables, trade and other accounts payables, loans and capital leases.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25">
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 144.6pt">As of December 31, 2018, the Company has a position in financial derivatives intended to hedge changes in the exchange rate of the USD vs. the NIS (see also f. below).</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 144.6pt"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">As of December 31, 2018, the Company has financial instruments, classified as </font>financial<font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"> assets measured at fair value through other comprehensive income for which the Company is exposed to risk of fluctuations in the security price that is determined by reference to the quoted market price.</font></div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 113.4pt">Financial instruments that potentially subject the Company to concentrations of credit risk consist principally of cash and cash equivalents, short-term bank deposits, marketable securities, trade receivables and foreign currency derivative contracts.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; line-height: 1.25">

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 144.6pt">The Company regularly monitors the credit extended to its customers and their general financial condition, and, when necessary, requires collateral as security for these debts such as letters of creditor and down payments. In addition, the Company partially insures its overseas sales with foreign trade risk insurance.</div>



<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 144.6pt">The Company keeps constant track of customer debt and the Financial Statements include an allowance for doubtful accounts that adequately reflects, in the Company's assessment, the loss embodied in the debts the collection of which is in doubt.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 144.6pt">The Company&#8217;s maximum exposure to credit risk for the components of the statement of financial position as of December 31, 2018 and 2017 is the carrying amount of trade receivables.</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 144.6pt">The Company holds cash, cash equivalents, short term deposits and other financial instruments at a major financial institutions in Israel. <font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">In accordance with Company policy, evaluations of </font>the relative strength of credit of the various financial institutions are made on an ongoing basis.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 144.6pt"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif">Short-term </font>investments<font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"> include short-term deposits with low risk for a period less than one year. The Company&#8217;s marketable securities consist of investment-grade corporate bonds, government bonds (Including U.S., Israeli and other government bonds). The Company&#8217;s investment policy, limits the amount the Company may invest in any one type of investment or issuer and the average maturities of the bond portfolio, thereby reducing credit risk concentrations.</font></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 144.6pt">The Company has not experienced any significant losses on its short term investments.</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt"><u>Sensitivity tests and principal work assumptions</u></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The selected changes in the relevant risk variables were determined based on management's estimate as to reasonable possible changes in these risk variables.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The Company has performed sensitivity tests of principal market risk factors that are liable to affect its reported operating results or financial position. The sensitivity tests present the profit or loss in respect of each financial instrument for the relevant risk variable chosen for that instrument as of each reporting date. The test of risk factors was determined based on the materiality of the exposure of the operating results or financial condition of each risk with reference to the functional currency and assuming that all the other variables are constant</div>

<div style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Derivatives and hedging:</u></div>
</td>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt"><u>Derivatives instruments not designated as hedging</u></div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The Company has foreign currency forward contracts designed to protect it from exposure to fluctuations in exchange rates, mainly of NIS and EUR, in respect of its&#160; trade receivables, trade payables and inventory. Foreign currency forward contracts are not designated as cash flow hedges, fair value or net investment in a foreign operation. These derivatives are not considered as hedge accounting. As of December 31, 2018 the fair value of the derivative instruments not designated as hedging was a liability of $6 thousands. The open transactions for those derivatives were in an amount of $5,009 thousands.</div>

<br style="line-height: 1.25" />
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt"><font style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, serif"><u>Cash flow hedges</u></font>:</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">As of December&#160;31, 2018, the Company held NIS/USD hedging contracts (cylinder contracts) designated as hedges of expected future salaries expenses and for expected future purchases from Israeli suppliers.</div>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
</div>

<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt">The main terms of these positions were set to match the terms of the hedged items. As of December 31, 2018 the fair value of the derivative instruments designated as hedge accounting was a liability of $58 thousands. The open transactions for those derivatives were in an amount of $1,169 thousands.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 85.05pt; line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
<div style="font: 10pt/1.25 Times New Roman,Times,serif; text-align: justify">Cash flow hedges of the expected salaries expenses in December 31, 2018 was estimated as highly effective and accordingly a net unrecognized loss was recorded in&#160; other comprehensive income in the amount of $99 thousands.</div>
</div></div></div></div></div></div></div><span></span>
</td>

<div style="line-height: 1.25"><br style="line-height: 1.25" />
